quote_candidates.quote: # Smartsheet MCP Server now generally available!

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: You can now connect Smartsheet to any MCP-compliant AI tool through the new Smartsheet MCP Server — an open, protocol-based integration layer built on Anthropic's Model Context Protocol standard.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: The MCP Server routes requests through Smartsheet REST API, pulling structured data with rich metadata — row relationships, column types, cell history, comments — all respecting the authenticated user's permissions.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: The MCP Server is also engineered with proprietary data optimization that compresses and filters payloads, so teams get faster AI responses at lower token costs as usage scales.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Ask "What are the top blockers in Q3?" or "Summarize project risks for exec review" and get contextually rich, intelligent responses.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: With the MCP Server, AI tools surface risks before they escalate and take approved actions — all governed by organization-level controls.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: The MCP Server is open by design.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: It works with any MCP-compliant client — commercial AI assistants like Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, etc., custom enterprise AI platforms, open-source agent frameworks, or internal copilots.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: One standardized endpoint, no vendor lock-in.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: And as Smartsheet's API capabilities expand, the MCP Server ensures AI tools keep pace automatically.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: **How to get started:** To use the Smartsheet MCP Server, you'll need:

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: * A Smartsheet Business or Enterprise plan

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: **Get connected:** If you're already building on the Smartsheet API, you have the foundation — the MCP Server leverages the same REST API infrastructure, authentication model, and data structures you already work with.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Connect your first MCP-compliant AI tool today.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.quote: ## Let your AI agents interact with the Stripe API by using our MCP server.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: The Stripe Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provides tools that AI agents can use to interact with the Stripe API and search the Stripe knowledge base, including documentation and support articles.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: ## Set up Stripe MCP with a plugin Recommended

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Agent plugins for Stripe automatically configure the Stripe MCP server, install our skills, and make sure they’re up to date.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Install the Stripe CLI using the installation script for your operating system.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: If your MCP client doesn’t support agent plugins for Stripe, or you prefer to configure the Stripe MCP server and install the skills manually, follow these instructions:

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Run the following command to add the Stripe MCP server to Claude Code:

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: claude mcp add --transport http stripe https://mcp.stripe.com/

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: After you add the server, start Claude Code and run the `/mcp` command to authenticate Stripe with OAuth.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: To authenticate with an agent API key instead of OAuth, add the server to your project’s `.mcp.json` file and reference an environment variable that holds your agent API key, rather than passing the key on the command line.

quote_candidates.quote: ## Manage MCP access and sessions

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Stripe’s MCP server supports two authentication methods:

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: **OAuth**: Use OAuth when a client accesses Stripe on behalf of your Stripe user account.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: **Agent API keys**: Use an agent API key when an AI application needs independent, persistent access to Stripe.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: When you connect an MCP client with OAuth, the client opens Stripe’s OAuth consent page.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: See the MCP authorization specification for details.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: OAuth refresh tokens expire after 14 days, and refreshing tokens doesn’t extend the session beyond 14 days from your initial authorization.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: When your session expires, reconnect your MCP client to Stripe and authorize it again.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: If your organization manages your device or network, your IT administrator might block connections to external MCP servers.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: When the Stripe MCP server doesn’t connect in a managed environment, ask your IT department to allow `mcp.stripe.com`.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: ### Manage MCP access for all team members

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: If you’re an administrator, you can enable or disable MCP access for your entire team in the Dashboard.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Configure access separately for live mode and sandbox environments.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Your authorized MCP clients appear under **OAuth sessions** in your user settings.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Find the client in the **OAuth sessions** list.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Find the **OAuth sessions** table.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Session management applies only to the account or organization and environment—live mode or a sandbox—that you’re currently viewing.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Revoking a session removes access only within that scope.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: The session remains active for accounts outside your current scope.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Use OAuth for interactive MCP clients.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: OAuth lets you authorize and revoke a client without sharing an API key.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: For autonomous clients that can’t use OAuth, create an agent API key with only the permissions the client needs.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: You can identify agent API keys in the Dashboard by the **Agent** badge.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Pass the agent API key as the bearer token in the `Authorization` header of your request.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: If you’re replacing an existing key, test the new configuration in a sandbox, then expire the old key.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: #### Update API key authentication before January 11, 2027

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Starting January 11, 2027, Stripe MCP will no longer accept full-access secret keys or non-agent restricted API keys.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Migrate to an agent API key or reconnect with OAuth before that date.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Requests using an unsupported key receive a `401` response with an OAuth discovery challenge.

quote_candidates.quote: ## Manage MCP access and sessions

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Stripe’s MCP server supports two authentication methods:

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: **OAuth**: Use OAuth when a client accesses Stripe on behalf of your Stripe user account.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: **Agent API keys**: Use an agent API key when an AI application needs independent, persistent access to Stripe.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: See the MCP authorization specification for details.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: OAuth refresh tokens expire after 14 days, and refreshing tokens doesn’t extend the session beyond 14 days from your initial authorization.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: When your session expires, reconnect your MCP client to Stripe and authorize it again.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Find the **OAuth sessions** table.

quote_candidates.quote: Session management applies only to the account or organization and environment—live mode or a sandbox—that you’re currently viewing.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Revoking a session removes access only within that scope.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: #### Update API key authentication before January 11, 2027

quote_candidates.quote: ## Exchange the authorization code for an access token

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Your callback URL receives an OAuth authorization code parameter that your back end needs to exchange for an API access token and the refresh token.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: This authorization code is one-time use only and valid only for 5 minutes, in which your back end needs to exchange the code for the access token.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: You’ll get a new refresh token and the previous refresh token expires.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.quote: ### Token models and types (the what)

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: **User-scoped access token:** A token issued to Plaid that enables Plaid to efficiently provision access to multiple third-party apps with a single token.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: This benefits users by providing a seamless experience for returning users and by reducing the need for repeated authorization steps.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: It also reduces API requests for consumers connecting multiple apps, streamlining management for Data Providers.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: You may also see this called an *aggregator token*, *single token*, or *universal token* in other Plaid materials; they all describe the same model.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: **Access token:** Short-lived (15 min) token for API access.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: **Refresh token:** Long-lived token used to obtain new access tokens.

quote_candidates.quote: #### Your guide to building a secure, standards-based OAuth integration with Plaid Core Exchange

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: * Why OAuth is essential for Core Exchange

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Plaid Core Exchange supports any spec-compliant OAuth 2.0 implementation, and strongly recommends OpenID Connect (OIDC), an identity layer built on OAuth 2.0.

quote_candidates.quote: ### Token models and types (the what)

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: **User-scoped access token:** A token issued to Plaid that enables Plaid to efficiently provision access to multiple third-party apps with a single token.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: This benefits users by providing a seamless experience for returning users and by reducing the need for repeated authorization steps.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review

quote_candidates.quote: If you're evaluating AI for your finance stack right now, your Request For Proposal (RFP) has a row for it: “MCP support ✓”.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is the standard way an AI agent connects to a system like your finance platform.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Anyone armed with a coding agent can stand up a working MCP server in under a week.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: The quick way is to put a thin layer over your existing API so an AI can reach it.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: The rest of this post is how we got there, and what to ask any vendor with the MCP checkmark.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Most of what ships today is the fast version: a thin wrapper around an existing API, dressed up so an AI can reach it.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: And how a vendor's MCP server handles that question, at both ends of that range, tells you almost everything about whether the thing behind the checkmark was built for scale or just built fast.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: **Approach one: the API wrapper:**

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: This is the thin version from a moment ago: the MCP server wraps the existing endpoints, pulls the raw expense records, and hands them to the LLM to sort out.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: In practical terms, a standard 200,000-token context window can comfortably hold around 500 expenses with room to spare; a larger 1-million-token window, 3,000 to 4,000.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Instead of dumping raw records into the model's context window, the agent pulls your data out of the API, transforms it, and loads it into a temporary in-memory database, then runs a SQL query against that.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: It's a genuinely better design than the API wrapper approach.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: For a company with thousands of expenses, "load the data" means paginating through the API 10, 20, 30 times, pulling every record across the wire before anything can be computed.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: The question worth asking is how the data actually moves through the MCP, because that's the real tell for how it was built.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Underneath Brex's MCP server, a change-data-capture pipeline streams every update from the source systems as it happens and reshapes it into denormalized tables built for querying, so the expensive joins are already resolved and the data sits ready.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: When the agent needs an answer, it doesn't paginate through an API or load anything into a table.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: It's schema-aware, ontology-aware, and permission-aware, and it returns answers rather than raw data.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: "Supports MCP" is one label for two very different philosophies.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: The other does the heavy lifting ahead of time, so the answer is already waiting: exact, current, permission-scoped.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Building the version that's fast, exact, and permission-safe at scale is the hard part, and it's the part a comparison chart can't show you.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: When you evaluate AI for finance, don't ask whether a vendor supports MCP.

quote_candidates.quote: Instead of dumping raw records into the model's context window, the agent pulls your data out of the API, transforms it, and loads it into a temporary in-memory database, then runs a SQL query against that.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: ## What MCP is and how we used it

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open-source standard developed by Anthropic that enables applications to expose data and functionality to LLMs.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: MCP provides an LLM with access to pretty much anything you want: databases, your computer’s filesystem, Figma, GitHub, etc.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Given that Ramp’s developer API is the primary way to access Ramp’s resources externally, we wanted to see what would happen if we put the two together.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: An MCP server in Python can be built using `FastMCP`.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: MCP "tools" are akin to HTTP endpoints the LLM can access through an MCP client.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: The following piece of code, for example, is reminiscent of a `Flask` HTTP endpoint decorated with `@app.route(…)` and OpenAPI spec schemas.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: @mcp.tool(…) # tool name or function name used to annotate tool name

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: results = await some_api(...) # expose your filesystem, some REST API, DB, etc.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: mcp.run(transport='stdio') # available with stdio or SSE transport

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Using `FastMCP` and a lightweight Ramp developer API client, we were able to build a working early prototype of the Ramp MCP server.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: With Claude Desktop as our MCP client, Claude was able to both generate visualizations and run simple analyses on spend data pulled from Ramp’s APIs using natural language.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Adding a new source of data *— like a different API endpoint —* was as simple as defining a new tool.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Our initial setup worked fine on a small demo business, but we quickly ran into a few scaling issues: miscalculations, limited context windows, input size limits, and high input token usage.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Thanks to the reduced token usage in this approach, Ramp MCP now even worked with the free version of Claude.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Everything aside from Developer API is running locally

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: In order to implement a SQL interface to analyze our API data, we built a lightweight in-memory ETL that pulls data from our APIs, transforms it, and loads it into an in-memory SQLite database.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: To transform our RESTful API’s JSON responses into SQL rows, we flattened the JSON and inferred the appropriate SQL column type based on the value types.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: As a solve, we added an interface to an OLAP-powered API built by our data platform team.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: `load_transactions`) to pull data from the Ramp API

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: A `process_data` tool to transform the data from the API and load into the SQLite table (we could've skipped this step to reduce roundtrips)

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: With these changes, the latency for extracting data from the API became the largest bottleneck as tool calls started timing out.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: LLMs are significantly better at SQL than at math, which is why this set of tools made sense for our RESTful API to expose relational spend data effectively.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: MCP allows you to create whatever interface works best for the type of data you want to connect to it, and it's on you to tinker a bit to figure out what the best data access strategy is.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: ## Where Ramp MCP shines (and where it breaks down)

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Our open-source `ramp-mcp` server can access a business context using a variety of tools, and enable natural language access to your Ramp data.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: There's the occasional reliability issue, and API latency can be high for very large businesses with a lot of data.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: There are plenty of optimizations we could implement (concurrent requests, pulling data from the APIs asynchronously, smart caching, using DuckDB, etc.), but building a scalable, and truly reliable agentic AI requires a great deal of complex technical work beyond what MCP currently offers.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: MCP and similar technologies can introduce information security risk if left unchecked.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: This means authentication credentials like API keys need to be secured, and following the principle of least privilege is as crucial as ever.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: As a mitigant, we implemented audit logging and you can pick a constrained set of OAuth scopes and tools to make available to the MCP client.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Audit logs for the Ramp developer API

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: MCP is early, with many limitations to overcome, and also a strong and growing community of engineers that can see the tip of the iceberg for how transformative this technology can be.

quote_candidates.source_type: cached official-domain candidate; vendor affiliation still requires review
quote_candidates.quote: Many MCP servers have been made available by businesses and enthusiasts alike, and anyone can connect their MCP client to a wide range of tools in their tech stack.
